title: 2019 AMC 10B Problem 18
statement: Henry decides one morning to do a workout, and he walks \(\tfrac{3}{4}\) of the way from his home to his gym. The gym is \(2\) kilometers away from Henry’s home. At that point, he changes his mind and walks \(\tfrac{3}{4}\) of the way from where he is back toward home. When he reaches that point, he changes his mind again and walks \(\tfrac{3}{4}\) of the distance from there back toward the gym. If Henry keeps changing his mind when he has walked \(\tfrac{3}{4}\) of the distance toward either the gym or home from the point where he last changed his mind, he will get very close to walking back and forth between a point \(A\) kilometers from home and a point \(B\) kilometers from home. What is \(|A-B|?\)

solutions.text:
Suppose a limiting homeward turnaround point is \(x\) kilometers from home. After Henry walks toward the gym, his position is \[2-\frac{2-x}{4}=\frac32+\frac{x}{4}.\]

After he turns back toward home, one quarter of that distance remains, so his next homeward turnaround point is \[\frac14\left(\frac32+\frac{x}{4}\right)=\frac38+\frac{x}{16}.\]

At the limiting point this two-step map leaves the position unchanged, so \[x=\frac38+\frac{x}{16},\] which gives \(x=\frac25\).

The other limiting point is the position reached after walking toward the gym: \[2-\frac{2-\frac25}{4}=\frac85.\] Therefore \[|A-B|=\frac85-\frac25=\frac65=1\frac15.\]

Thus, the correct answer is C .
hints: Study the two-step map from one turnaround point back to the same direction
At the limiting point, applying that two-step map changes nothing
